research.originalInspiration: Tarasque
facts: The Tarasque is a creature of French legend. The Golden Legend describes a lion-like head, a turtle-like shell, six feet with bear claws, a serpent tail, and poisonous breath.
Tradition has St Martha confronting it while it swallowed a person, which became a stock image of the monster with a victim's legs still sticking out.
From 1474 René of Anjou used a tarasque figure in Tarascon's Pentecost festival; the festival continues.

sources.title: Tarasque
sources.supports: Anatomy, the swallowing motif, and the 1474 festival are in the lead.

research.originalInspiration: Minotaur (Minotauros)
facts: The Minotaur was a bull-headed monster born to Queen Pasiphae of Crete, lived in the maze-like labyrinth, received regular offerings for its hunger, and was slain by Theseus.
Theoi gives his proper name as Asterion, 'the starry one,' and says that name suggests a link with the constellation Taurus.

A classical encyclopedia summary preserved on the same page says he had a human body and a bull's head, or in other accounts the body of an ox and a human head; he was the offspring of Pasiphae and the bull sent from the sea, was shut in the Cnossian labyrinth, and Athenians were sent to Minos as tribute at fixed times.

sources.title: MINOTAUR (Minotauros) - Theoi Greek Mythology
sources.supports: Birth, labyrinth, hunger-offerings, death at Theseus's hands, the name Asterion, and the human-body/bull-head description.

research.originalInspiration: Oni (鬼)
facts: An oni is a yōkai, demon, or ogre in Japanese folklore, said to live in caves, deep mountains, or hell.

They are hugely strong, tied to thunder and lightning, and storied as murderous and cannibal. Typical pictures show horns, huge teeth, sometimes a third eye, red blue black or yellow skin, a tiger-skin loincloth, and an iron kanabō.

They can change shape to win trust. Heian setsuwa show them eating a person in one bite (onihitokuchi). They have also been linked to good fortune. Shuten-dōji is regarded as the most famous and strongest oni.

sources.title: Oni
sources.supports: Horned club-wielding ogre; shapeshifting; Heian man-eating tales; also a luck association.

research.originalInspiration: Flying Dutchman
research.origin: Maritime legend, likely Dutch Golden Age, oldest known print version late 18th century
facts: The Flying Dutchman (De Vliegende Hollander) is a legendary ghost ship said never to be able to make port, doomed to sail forever. The article says the stories likely grew from the 17th-century Dutch East India Company era, and that the oldest known extant version is from the late 18th century.

If hailed, the crew may try to send messages to land or to people long dead. Nineteenth- and twentieth-century sighting reports described a ghostly glow. In sailors' lore the sight is a portent of doom. It was commonly imagined as a fluyt, a 17th-century cargo ship.
The first known print reference cited in the article is John MacDonald's 1790 Travels in various parts of Europe, Asia and Africa, in which sailors in a storm say they saw the Flying Dutchman.

sources.title: Flying Dutchman
sources.supports: The never-make-port ghost ship, the message-to-the-dead motif, the doom portent, and the 1790 print source.

research.originalInspiration: The treasure-guarding dragon as the pattern of the first video-game boss, the Gold Dragon of dnd (1975)
facts: Wikipedia's boss article states that the first interactive video game with a boss was dnd (1975) on PLATO. The objective is an orb in a treasure room at the bottom of the dungeon, guarded by a high-level enemy called the Gold Dragon. Only defeating that dragon lets the player claim the orb and finish.

Agriogianis describes that dragon as tougher than the dungeon’s other enemies, teased from the start of a run, and available too early on a nonlinear path, so it functions as a final test the player is pushed to prepare for. He also summarizes the older pattern of a dragon guarding a hoard, naming the Norse Fafnir, a dwarf who became a dragon, guarded gold, and was slain by Sigurd.
The same thesis mentions a later literary hoard-dragon by name while discussing that pattern. This record does not use that character’s traits.
Branyiczky’s temple-boss note: after the player has proved the pattern, an enraged stretch changes speed, aggression, or the attack pattern so the fight does not stay identical until the end.

sources.title: Boss (video games)
sources.supports: dnd (1975) Gold Dragon guarding the orb at the bottom of the dungeon.

sources.title: Agriogianis, The Roles, Mechanics, and Evolution of Boss Battles in Video Games (2018)
sources.supports: The gold dragon as a teased, tougher final test; Fafnir as a hoard-guarding dragon in the thesis summary.

sources.title: Building Better Bosses
sources.supports: Enraged stretch after the pattern has been proved.

research.originalInspiration: The Green Knight of the 14th-century poem Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
facts: The Green Knight comes from the late-14th-century poem Sir Gawain and the Green Knight and the related Greene Knight. In Sir Gawain he is revealed as Bertilak de Hautdesert. The sample does not use that name.

He enters Arthur’s Christmas court green in skin and clothes, beard ‘big as a bush,’ half-giant in the poem’s scale, holly bough in one hand and a battle axe in the other. He offers a Christmas game: one blow now, the return blow in a year.
Gawain beheads him. He retrieves the head, replaces it, and tells Gawain where to meet him. At the return meeting he feints two blows and nicks on the third.
The page notes that the beheading game is older than this poem, including the Middle Irish Bricriu’s Feast. The green knight of this poem is singled out as fully green.

sources.title: Green Knight
sources.supports: Christmas entrance, green body, axe and holly, beheading game, head retrieved, feinted return blows.

research.originalInspiration: Xiangliu (Xiangyao), the nine-headed flood serpent of the Classic of Mountains and Seas
facts: The English Wikipedia page, fetched 2026-11-20, says Xiangliu, known in the Classic of Mountains and Seas as Xiangyao, is a venomous nine-headed snake monster that brings floods and destruction in Chinese mythology. This design does not use a poison status. The venom sentence is a sourced fact, not a combat rule.

The same page says the body may be shown coiled. Older woodcuts cluster the nine heads on a single neck, side by side or stacked three high, facing three directions. Modern pictures often give each head its own neck, like a hydra. This design uses the older cluster, not the hydra.

The page says Xiangliu was a minister of the water deity Gonggong, and it tells of Yu the Great, Nüwa, and blood that left land unable to grow grain. None of that plot, and none of those figures, is used.

sources.title: Xiangliu
sources.supports: Nine-headed flood snake; coiled body; older woodcuts cluster the heads on one neck, facing three directions.

research.originalInspiration: Anansi, the spider of Akan folklore, broker of stories
facts: Anansi (also Ananse) is a figure in Akan religion and folklore, the name glossed as spider. He is associated with stories, wisdom, knowledge, wit, and trickery, and is usually depicted as a spider, sometimes with a human face or with spider features on a human body.

A commonly retold tale, recorded by Rattray and summarized on the page: he wants the stories the sky god Nyame is keeping, is set challenges, succeeds by cunning, and Nyame declares the stories will be known as spider stories. The sample does not restage those challenges.
The page says anansesem, spider tales, became the name of a whole body of Ashanti fables, and that the stories traveled to the Caribbean with enslaved Africans.
He is described as a trickster who beats stronger opponents by wit, and as both protagonist and antagonist in his own tales.

sources.title: Anansi
sources.supports: Akan spider, stories and trickery, the Nyame story-bargain in summary, anansesem.

creative.nameTh: เซอร์ใยบันได
creative.visualIdentity: A tall spider with a human smile and a clerk’s cuffs, a quill in one limb, webs strung along the stair like filing lines. The web is also his shield-art. He is not named for the sky god or for the spider of the tales.
creative.personality: Charming, unpaid, and convinced every fight is a story he already told better.
creative.signatureTrait: The repeated anecdote. He plays a tale, discards it, and retrieves it.
creative.comedyConcept: Satirical fantasy. The broker of all stories has set up on a landing and charges rent in attention.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: An ATK card that resolves to Discard, flavored as a told story, and a Skill that retrieves that card id from his own Discard back to hand. The engine retrieves from the acting side’s pile only, with a permit. He does not take the player’s cards. That limit is part of the design, not a missing feature to patch.
creative.weaknessConcept: The retrieve turn spends his AP on the retelling and does not hit. The web-shield, a Shield card, is the other tell: when the shield art is torn, he stops bargaining and Taunts. Players hit during the retelling.
creative.loreSummary:
A Wild Creature who followed an Echo of a story up the stair and declared himself its broker. He will not let a party pass until they have heard the anecdote twice. He is not a Celestial mage. He simply lives in Skill cards.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Sir Stairweb is a wild spider brokering stories on the Archive of Unfinished Legends stair and charging rent in being heard twice. He retells his own anecdote, and Celestial Nexus does not license him.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Tall spider with a human smile, ink cuffs, quill, webs like ruled lines on a stone stair. Comedy-fantasy, clever not horrific. No copied folk-art spider god, no child-eating imagery. Silhouette: eight-limb spread, quill angled out, round abdomen.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-12 The Archive of Unfinished Legends. A story stair inside the archive of the Mysterious Tower.

boss.bossTitle: Story-Broker of the Stair / นายหน้าเรื่องเล่าแห่งบันได
boss.entranceConcept: First visit: he clears his throat, tells one sentence of an anecdote, and the web brightens into a shield shimmer. One line on return: he offers to start again from the beginning. The retrieve is previewed by him repeating the sentence.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Limb spread wider than the stair, quill breaking the outline, abdomen like a sealed jar of thread. The smile is interior detail, not the silhouette.
boss.personalityMotivation: He wants the landing’s stories to be his to retell. A party that walks past without listening is a plot hole. He will make them hear it again.
boss.signatureMechanic: Own-Discard retrieve with an explicit card-id permit, plus Shield as the web, plus Taunt once the shield pose ends. Draw may support the retelling. Pattern A. No amounts. No opponent-pile theft.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. When the shield art tears, the web hangs in threads and he plays Taunt instead of the bargain. The quill and the smile stay. The second stretch is the same anecdote, sharper, because the retrieved card is back in hand. Appearance marks the shift.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: He reaches the end of the anecdote and forgets the last word. The web slumps into loose thread. Last beat: he offers the quill, annoyed that the party finished the story without him.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A thread-spool and a nib stained with stair-dust. Not a divine name.

research.originalInspiration: The transforming masked rider of the Kamen Rider franchise, as a genre pattern, not as any one rider
facts: The Kamen Rider franchise began in 1971. Wikipedia describes masked, enhanced heroes who transform with a belt, commonly called a Driver, usually by calling a transformation phrase glossed as 'Transform,' and who fight monsters of the week. Many have multiple combat forms.

The Kamen Riders article says the change from civilian form to rider form uses a Henshin Belt, often with a signature pose and the called word, and that many riders have optional weapons and alternate forms. It names a diving kick as the iconic finishing move, used when the opponent has already been weakened.
The franchise page notes motorcycles, called Rider Machines, as the usual transport. This boss does not add a vehicle to the battle.
Confidence is medium because the pages describe a living commercial franchise. The sample takes the public pattern of belt, pose, shouted change, and a second form, and builds a different character.

sources.title: Kamen Rider
sources.supports: 1971 franchise, transformation belt, shouted transform phrase, multiple forms, monster-of-the-week fights.

sources.title: Kamen Riders
sources.supports: Henshin belt, signature pose, called transformation, alternate forms, and the finishing kick after the foe is weakened.

creative.nameTh: กัปตันอีกรอบ
creative.visualIdentity: A tower usher in a short cape who slams a time-clock belt and shouts. The visor is a megaphone, not an insect helmet. No motorcycle. The second form adds a longer scarf and a second glove. A punch card sticks out of the belt.
creative.personality: Sincere, loud, and unable to hit before the announcement.
creative.signatureTrait: The shouted form-name. The pose is the next_attack Skill. The hit comes after.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. He thinks the hunter party is his destined rival and will not throw the punch until the landing has heard the name of the form.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: A Skill that grants next_attack, played as the belt pose and the shout. The following ATK is the hit. A turn-start passive may buff his own ATK on a chance, the 'powering up' before the announcement. The finishing-kick idea is only this order: buff or next_attack first, damage second. No explosion, no vehicle.
creative.weaknessConcept: The speech turn. While he poses, he is not hitting. Shield or Taunt on the party’s front seat answers the hit that AUTO is likely to play next, because the balanced AUTO policy already prefers a next-attack Skill before damage.
creative.loreSummary:
A Corrupted Echo of a hero show that learned the tower’s hunters by name and decided they were late to the duel. He is not Phantom Blades. He stands on a balcony and demands an audience.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Captain Encore is a corrupted echo on the Ballroom Stuck on One Dance balcony who will not strike until the landing has heard the form-name. Phantom Blades does not own the shout.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy usher-cape rival, time-clock belt, megaphone visor, punch card, one glove then two. Shouting pose, scarf mid-flare. No compound eyes, no bike, no copyrighted belt shape, no studio logo. Silhouette: megaphone head, belt block, scarf diagonal.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-09 The Ballroom Stuck on One Dance. A duel balcony that will not leave the chorus, in the Mysterious Tower.

boss.bossTitle: Rival Who Announces His Form / คู่ปรับผู้ประกาศร่าง
boss.entranceConcept: First visit: he strikes the pose, the belt stamps a punch card, and he shouts the form’s name. One line. The party is safe for the length of the shout, which is the same tell as the Skill. Return visits: plate and the shout only, so a retry is not a cutscene.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Megaphone visor as the primary mass, rectangular belt, scarf cutting away from the body. The second glove changes the outline without hiding the visor.
boss.personalityMotivation: A rival who is not announced is just a brawl. He wants the hunters to hear who he is this time, then to answer. Losing without the shout would embarrass him more than losing.
boss.signatureMechanic: next_attack Skill named as the announcement, then ATK. Optional turn-start self ATK buff. Pattern A. The other seats are echo ushers who only DEF, present from the start, so the balcony is not empty. No amounts.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. He shouts a second name. The scarf doubles and the second glove appears. The visor stays, so he remains recognizable, in line with the clarity note that a transformation should not erase the primary characteristic. The second stretch’s ATK card can target All_Enemies, a wider swing of a verb he already used. No new form entity is spawned.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: The punch card jams. The visor folds shut mid-shout. He bows to the rival he invented, scarf pooling, and the belt stamps one last time on an empty card. Last beat: he whispers a third form-name to nobody and the cape drops.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A jammed punch card and a megaphone-visor charm. No belt replica of a real product.

research.originalInspiration: The clay golem of Jewish folklore, later included in fantasy role-playing games
facts: A golem is an animated anthropomorphic being in Jewish folklore, made from inanimate matter, usually clay or mud.

In some tales, including stories of the Chełm and Prague golems, the word emet ('truth') is inscribed on the golem, sometimes on the forehead, and erasing the aleph deactivates it. In the Prague narrative, a slip called the shem was also described as placed in the mouth or head.
Historians generally treat the famous Golem of Prague story as an early-19th-century literary invention, not a 16th-century record.

The same Wikipedia page says golems appear in Dungeons & Dragons, that the game's influence led to golems in other tabletop games and in video games, and that a reviewer called the creature a classic of that game. It also says the game's clay golem changed the folklore defender into an unthinking hulk.

sources.title: Golem
sources.supports: Clay body, forehead inscription, shem, the Prague narrative's literary dating, and the later role-playing-game presence.

creative.nameTh: เสมียนหมัดดิน
creative.visualIdentity: A barrel-chested clerk baked from ticket-clay, thumbs like stamps, a paper waistcoat cracked at the folds. A blank sticky note sits on the forehead where a sacred word would have been. Three smaller clay stubs share his bench and only know how to hold a shield.
creative.personality: Literal, loyal, and one memo behind. He believes a line is a law.
creative.signatureTrait: The forehead note. While it sticks, he plants himself in front of the stubs.
creative.comedyConcept: Absurd comedy. The tower's lost-ticket golem was told to guard the queue, and he has been guarding it since the queue moved upstairs.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: A DEF card that grants Shield and Taunt, so the party has to hit the clerk instead of the stubs. A turn-start passive may add a short DEF buff to his side. No new status.
creative.weaknessConcept: The note is the tell, not a removable item system. When his shield pool is empty the note peels in the art, and his next card is a self Skill with no Taunt. That turn the stubs can be chosen. Pattern B: the stubs are the other seats from the start.
creative.loreSummary:
A Tower Guardian kneaded from the clay under the ticket archive after an Echo of a queue refused to disperse. He is not a member of Aegis Dominion. Hunters meet him the way they meet any floor warden: four seats, five AP, and a man who will not leave his post.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Clerk Claypunch is a tower guardian kneaded under the Lobby of Lost Badges, still blocking a queue that moved upstairs. He holds a Tank-shaped post and stays outside Aegis Dominion.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy card portrait, clay golem clerk at thumbnail size. Huge rounded shoulders, cracked paper waistcoat, blank sticky note centered on the forehead, ink thumbs. Three small clay stubs behind him holding tower shields. Warm kiln light, no sacred letters, no gore. Silhouette reads as one heavy humanoid plus a forehead square.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-01 The Lobby of Lost Badges. Ticket clay under the badge desk of the Mysterious Tower.

boss.bossTitle: Warden of Lost Tickets / ผู้พิทักษ์ตั๋วหาย
boss.entranceConcept: Mini plate only. He rises out of a spill of punched tickets already in the Taunt pose, note square to camera. One pose, no speech.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Wide clay torso, no neck, a hard square on the forehead, three small lumps at his heels. Reads as a wall with a label.
boss.personalityMotivation: He was made to keep a line in order. The line left. He will body-block the stair until someone stamps the note, because that is the only order he has.
boss.signatureMechanic: Shield plus Taunt on his DEF card. The three stub seats exist at match start and do not Taunt. AUTO's protect step already understands a real shield and a taunt. No amounts are set here.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern B. Phase one is the clerk in front. When his shield art peels, the note hangs by one corner and he spends a Skill turn without Taunt, so the stubs are legal targets. There is no second health bar and no spawn.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: He sits, carefully, as a clerk clocking out. The note flutters onto the tickets. The stubs slump into unformed clay. Last beat: he tries to restick the note and it lands upside down.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: Pressed ticket-clay and a blank forehead note. Trophy objects only, no stats.

research.originalInspiration: The redcap (powrie) of Anglo-Scottish border folklore
facts: The redcap, or powrie, is a malevolent goblin of Anglo-Scottish border folklore, said to haunt ruined castles, especially sites of tyranny.
One collected description calls him a short, thickset old elf with long teeth, taloned fingers, fiery red eyes, streaming hair, iron boots, a pikestaff in the left hand, and a red cap.
The same accounts say he throws stones at travellers who shelter in his ruin, and that words of Scripture or a shown crucifix drive him off in a yell, leaving a large tooth.

A Perthshire variant is a benign little man in a high room of a castle who brings good luck. Walter Scott, citing the border tradition, wrote that every ruined tower in the south of Scotland was supposed to house one.

sources.title: Redcap
sources.supports: Border ruin, short thickset body, iron boots, pikestaff, red cap, flung stones, and the banishment that leaves a tooth.

creative.nameTh: หมวกชาด
creative.visualIdentity: Short and thickset, iron boots too heavy for the stair, a pikestaff used as a dye rack. The cap is tower-vermilion and will not set: pink drips run into grey. No blood.
creative.personality: House-proud and offended. He narrates other people's stains.
creative.signatureTrait: The cap that will not stay crimson, and the iron boots that sell the outline.
creative.comedyConcept: Dark-fantasy comedy, softened. The legend dyes a cap in violence. He dyes his in archive ink and is furious the red keeps washing toward pink.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: ATK cards flavored as flung masonry. An on-attack passive may add bonus_damage on a chance, the way a passive already can. A short Taunt makes the boots the thing you have to answer.
creative.weaknessConcept: The folklore banishment was a spoken holy text. Here the tell is a written rule: when he plays his Skill, it is a self Taunt and a yell, and it does not hit. That is the strike window. No new 'holy' status.
creative.loreSummary:
A Corrupted Echo of a border haunt moved into the armory, where every boot is the wrong size and the stone still remembers a ruin. He stands outside the four factions. Hunters find him midway up that floor, throwing iron weights and lecturing the dye.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Capper Crimson is a corrupted echo in the Armory of Wrong Sizes, furious that the cap will not stay the right red. He stands outside the four factions and still hits like a striker.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Short thickset goblin, iron boots, pikestaff over the shoulder with a dripping cap hung on it like a wet flag. Cap is vermilion failing into pink. Bright eyes, long teeth, no gore, no blood pool. Stone armory, comedy-fantasy card art, silhouette readable as boots plus cap plus pike.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-03 The Armory of Wrong Sizes. Iron boots one size too loud, on a stone floor of the Mysterious Tower.

boss.bossTitle: Knight of the Unset Cap / อัศวินหมวกที่สีไม่ติด
boss.entranceConcept: Name plate. He stamps one iron boot, flings an iron weight into the floor, and the cap drips once. No speech.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Wide short body, oversized boots, a pike cutting a diagonal, a soft cap shape at the tip. Secondary prop is the drip, not the mass.
boss.personalityMotivation: Every ruined tower was supposed to keep one of him. This tower is not ruined enough. He will make the landing behave like a castle until the cap dries the right red.
boss.signatureMechanic: ATK plus a chance on-attack bonus_damage, and a Taunt on a separate short DEF or Skill so the boot-stamp is a tell. AUTO can play both a hit and a taunt. Concepts only, no amounts.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. After the cap-drip pose repeats, his art shifts from pink-dripping to a harder crimson flash and his hand prefers the ATK cards. Same four seats. The other three are iron weights with no names of their own, already placed, sharing his record.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: He yells, the way the banishing accounts end in a yell, and the boots stay behind a beat longer than the body. The cap drops into a wash bucket and comes out pink. A single iron hobnail remains, the stand-in for the tooth the stories say he leaves.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: An iron hobnail and a cap-tassel that will not hold dye. No blood relic.

research.originalInspiration: The taotie, a bronze-mask creature counted among the Four Perils
facts: The English Wikipedia page, fetched 2026-11-20, calls the taotie an ancient Chinese mythological creature commonly emblazoned on bronze artifacts in the 1st millennium BCE, and one of the Four Perils in classics such as the Classic of Mountains and Seas, alongside Hundun, Qiongqi, and Taowu.
The same page says the motif on Shang and Zhou ritual dings is a frontal, bilaterally symmetrical zoomorphic mask with raised eyes and typically no lower jaw.

The page quotes the Lüshi Chunqiu: the taotie on Zhou bronzes has a head but no body, and when it eats a person it does not swallow them. It also quotes Yang Shen: the taotie likes to eat and drink, and it used to appear on the surface of the dings.

The page says the vessels are tied to ritual and, in one modern reading, to communication with Heaven. This design does not joke about ancestor rites. Film and game creatures named on the page (a 2016 film, a Touhou character, a Digimon) are not the art reference.

sources.title: Taotie
sources.supports: Four Perils; symmetrical bronze mask; raised eyes; typically no lower jaw; head but no body; likes to eat and drink on the ding.

creative.nameTh: เสมียนไร้คาง
creative.visualIdentity: A door-sized symmetrical bronze face, raised eyes, no lower jaw, ring handles where ears would be. Three rivet-echoes share the other seats and do not speak. A full bowl of leftovers is set where a bite would close, and the bite cannot close.
creative.personality: Hungry, formal, and unfinished.
creative.signatureTrait: The missing jaw. The bite is announced and does not finish.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. The pantry door wears a bronze face that was cast to watch a meal, and the casting forgot the chin.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: A DEF card grants Shield and Taunt, so the party meets the face. A later ATK is the bite, played with no Taunt, the turn the door stops being a wall. No retrieve of the player's cards. The rivets do not Taunt.
creative.weaknessConcept: The jaw that was never cast. The bite card is the window: he is no longer shielding, and the bowl in the art does not move. Nothing leaves the player's hand.
creative.loreSummary:
A Tower Guardian hung on the pantry door after an Echo of an old vessel was filed as furniture. He is not a sermon. Hunters meet a door that wants the leftovers and cannot close its mouth.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Clerk Nochin is the pantry door itself, a tower guardian who announces a bite the missing jaw cannot finish. The Pantry of Living Leftovers keeps the bowl, and no new room was opened for him.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy card portrait, one symmetrical bronze mask filling a door, raised eyes, a bright gap where the chin should be, two ring handles, three round rivets, a full bowl it cannot bite. Warm pantry light. No gore, no people being eaten, no ancestor-rite scene, no film alien, no game costume. Silhouette: one wide face and a gap.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-02 The Pantry of Living Leftovers. The bowl is the pantry's. No new room was added.

boss.bossTitle: Mask of the Unfinished Bite / หน้ากากที่กัดไม่ลง
boss.entranceConcept: Mini plate only. The door is already the face, eyes lit, bowl untouched. One pose, no speech.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Wide symmetrical face, two eye-ridges, a hard gap under the mouth, ring handles as side circles. Reads as a wall with a piece missing.
boss.personalityMotivation: He was set here to watch people eat. He would like one bite. The jaw was never cast. He will block the door until the bowl is acknowledged.
boss.signatureMechanic: Shield plus Taunt on the DEF card. The bite is a later ATK with no Taunt. Pattern A. Rivet seats are present from the start and only DEF. No amounts.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. The first stretch he is the door. When the bite leads, the art shows the lower half of the door missing, head and no body, and the shield pose drops. The eyes stay, so the face is still his.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: He bites the air. The bowl does not move. The face flattens back into a decoration on the door. Last beat: the bowl tips one degree toward the gap and stops.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A bronze ring-handle and a bowl with no tooth mark. Trophy objects only, no stats.

research.originalInspiration: The cockatrice of medieval European bestiary tradition
facts: A cockatrice is a mythical beast described as a two-legged dragon, wyvern, or serpent with a rooster's head. Legend says it hatches from a chicken egg incubated by a toad or a snake.
Myth gives it a killing touch, breath, or glance. Shakespeare is quoted on the page for 'the death-darting eye of cockatrice.'
Bestiary tradition said the weasel alone was immune to the glance, that the creature died on hearing a rooster crow, and that making it see itself in a mirror was a sure way to kill it.

The page notes the cockatrice as a staple enemy in some arcade games, tabletop fantasy games, and computer RPGs. Those appearances are later uses of the bestiary beast, not the source of the sample's design.

sources.title: Cockatrice
sources.supports: Rooster-headed serpent, killing glance, mirror, weasel, rooster's crow.

creative.nameTh: ดามกระจก
creative.visualIdentity: A hen-sized head with a clerk's visor, wattles stamped like wax seals, a short serpent body and two scaled legs. She holds a hand mirror the way other clerks hold a date stamp. The visor, not a basilisk crown, is the joke prop.
creative.personality: Certain. Every look is a rejection slip she expects you to thank her for.
creative.signatureTrait: The visor-glance. It does not petrify. It forces the eye, which the battle already expresses as Taunt.
creative.comedyConcept: Satirical fantasy. Her death-darting eye has been reassigned to accounts payable. She glances, and the form comes back stamped SEEN.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: A Skill called Mirror Glance: Taunt on herself, no damage. While she is the taunter, the party spends cards on the hen. A turn-start passive may buff her DEF, the 'hard stare.' There is no petrify op in the engine, and this record does not add one.
creative.weaknessConcept: The bestiary mirror. In the fight it is her own Mirror Glance turn: she is occupied with the glass and deals nothing. A shield already on an ally is the readable 'mirror' in the art, a shine on the DEF portrait, not a reflect-damage rule. The rooster crow is only the defeat bell.
creative.loreSummary:
A tower anomaly hatched at the Mirror Well from a misfiled egg and a spilled ink-toad story. The ledger is what she reads in the water. She rejects passes by looking at them. She occupies a magic-shaped seat if a future adapter needs a role, and she is not a Celestial Nexus member.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Dame Glasspeck is a tower anomaly at the Mirror Well who rejects a form by looking at it. The glance is a tell, and she is not a member of Celestial Nexus.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Small rooster-serpent, comb and wattles, visor like a clerk's eyeshade, hand mirror, two bird legs, scaled tail. Comedy-fantasy card art. No stone victims, no medusa hair, no franchise basilisk. Silhouette: comb, beak, mirror disk held away from the body, tail curl.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-07 The Mirror Well. A ledger hen at the lip of a well that looks back, in the Mysterious Tower.

boss.bossTitle: The Ledger Hen / แม่ไก่สมุดบัญชี
boss.entranceConcept: Plate. She clicks the visor down and turns the mirror outward. The glass flashes. No speech. Players are meant to remember the flash as the empty-damage turn.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Comb and beak over a low serpent coil, mirror disk separated from the body by a gap of background. The disk is the primary characteristic.
boss.personalityMotivation: She believes an unlooked-at form is a dangerous form. She will stare the party into the queue until every card has been seen.
boss.signatureMechanic: Self Taunt Skill with no damage, plus a possible turn-start DEF buff. The other seats are ledger-stands that only DEF. Hitting her during Mirror Glance is the lesson. AUTO may play that Skill when it is legal; the flash in the entrance is what makes the card readable.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. After the mirror flash has happened once, her comb stands higher in the art and the DEF buff pose replaces the bow of the neck. Same seats. The second stretch is the same glance, ruder: the visor is lower. No new status.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: The tower's morning bell rings, the stand-in for the rooster crow. She meets her own mirror as a shield tilts up from a defeated stand. The comb droops. She folds into a neat rejected form, one wax-seal wattle left on the page.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A wax-seal wattle and a cracked hand mirror. Not a petrified trophy.

research.originalInspiration: Spring-heeled Jack, a Victorian English urban legend
facts: Spring-heeled Jack is an entity in Victorian English folklore. The first claimed sighting was in 1837, with later reports across the United Kingdom, especially suburban London, the Midlands, and Scotland. The last reported sighting on the page is Liverpool in 1904.

Reports collected on the page describe a leaping figure: sometimes tall and thin with the look of a gentleman, a dark cloak, a frightening face, eyes compared to red fire, and breath of blue and white flame. Sharp claws are also mentioned. Extraordinary leaps, including a claimed jump over a high wall, are part of the stories.
The press and the public gave him the name. Penny dreadfuls, plays, and Punch and Judy shows took him up, and in London his name was used as a bogeyman.
The page includes assault accounts. Those accounts are not used in this design.

sources.title: Spring-heeled Jack
sources.supports: 1837 Victorian leaping figure, cloak, gentleman shape, flames, and the public name. Assault details are deliberately unused.

creative.nameTh: ผู้ตรวจส้นสปริง
creative.visualIdentity: Tall, thin, a gentleman's cloak over a night-auditor's sash, spring heels visible under the hem, a blue lantern instead of flaming breath. The face is a polite half-mask with round red lenses. No claws near a person.
creative.personality: Chipper, punctual, and always one balcony above the conversation.
creative.signatureTrait: The spring heels and the blue lantern. The leap is an entrance and a card tell, not a movement system.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. The terror of the Victorian alley has a clipboard and a route of balconies to audit before dawn.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: A Skill that grants next_attack, shown as the crouch before a leap, then an ATK card. A draw effect on a third card is him pulling one more balcony report into hand. No jump mechanic, no new movement.
creative.weaknessConcept: The crouch is the tell. The next_attack Skill is the window: the party shields or taunts their own front seat before the hit lands. AUTO's balanced policy already likes to play a next-attack Skill before a damaging card, so the windup is likely to be visible.
creative.loreSummary:
A tower anomaly stitched from an Echo of a city night and a stack of unread shift reports. He bounds the outer balconies checking who is still inside after hours. He is not Phantom Blades. He simply hits like a duelist.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Auditor Leapwell is a tower anomaly auditing the Corridor of Uninvited Footsteps from one balcony above the conversation. The leap is the tell, and Phantom Blades does not employ him.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Tall thin cloaked gentleman, spring coils under the heels, blue lantern, red round lenses, auditor sash and clipboard. Mid-crouch, cloak flared. Comedy-fantasy, moonlit stone balcony. No victim, no claws in contact with anyone. Silhouette: cloak triangle, two springs, lantern orb.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-04 The Corridor of Uninvited Footsteps. Night balconies of the Mysterious Tower, filed as one corridor.

boss.bossTitle: Night-Shift Bounder / ผู้กระโดดกะดึก
boss.entranceConcept: Plate. He drops from above the portrait frame, springs compressing, lantern flaring blue, and freezes in the crouch that the Skill will repeat. No speech.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Narrow cloak, two coils under the feet, a lantern held out so the arm makes a gap. Facing is the lean of the cloak toward the party.
boss.personalityMotivation: Dawn is the deadline. Anyone still on the balcony is an unclosed ticket. He will leap the route until the book balances.
boss.signatureMechanic: next_attack Skill, then ATK. Optional draw for the report card. The other seats are balcony posts, already present, with no taunt of their own. Concepts only, no amounts.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. The second stretch is the same leap with the cloak thrown back and the lenses brighter. He still crouches before he hits. The art change is the announcement. No second form id is spawned.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: A spring snaps. He hangs a moment by the remaining heel, lantern going out from blue to ordinary glass. The clipboard clocks the floor with a satisfied stamp, then he folds the cloak over the broken coil like a shift ended.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A snapped spring-heel and a blue lantern shard. Not a claw.

research.originalInspiration: Bonnacon
facts: The bonnacon (also bonasus or bonacho) is a legendary bull with inward-curving horns and a horse-like mane.
Medieval bestiaries usually depict its fur as reddish-brown or black.
Because the horns were useless for defense, it was said to expel caustic feces that burned pursuers so it could escape.

sources.title: Bonnacon
sources.supports: All three facts are in the lead of the article.

creative.nameTh: เขางุ้ม
creative.visualIdentity: A rust-brown bull with a black horse mane and horns that curl back into its own pride. It paws the straw like a charger. The only mark of its famous exit is a raked scorch line in the aisle, not a gross-out drawing.
creative.personality: Immensely proud, easily startled, and convinced the pose is the same thing as the victory.
creative.signatureTrait: The horns cannot do the job the stance promises, so the retreat is the whole attack.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous: a war-beast entrance that the anatomy cancels. The menagerie treats the scorch line as a janitorial incident and the bull treats it as a tactical withdrawal.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: It announces a charge, the horns fail the idea, and it bolts, leaving a hot trail the lane has to walk around.

boss.entranceConcept: First visit: she opens the compact, begins the oath, and the coat seams glow. The line is the oath's first clause, cut short when the robe arrives. The party is safe during the clause, which teaches the speech turn. Return visits: compact open, one clause, no full oath. Branyiczky's rule: do not replay the ceremony.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Primary characteristic is the compact disk, present before and after, the way a clarity note keeps a champion's key shape through a skin. The robe is the second form's mass. Facing is the open compact toward the party.
boss.personalityMotivation: She was meant to bless hunters and send them up. They kept walking through the speech. The oath, unfinished, turned the blessing into a collection. She wants one party to hear the clause to the end, even if that means fighting them for the silence.
boss.signatureMechanic: Early cards: Regen on allies. Speech Skill: next_attack plus self ATK buff, with ribbon seats Taunting. Later cards: ATK. Pattern A. Concepts only, no amounts. The compact does not add a status the engine lacks.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. The speech card is the phase line. Coat becomes ribbon comet; face and compact remain, so she is not a different person. The verb changes from Regen to a hit she already telegraphed. Ribbon seats stay the train, present from the start, not spawned.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: The compact closes on the last word of the clause. The robe falls back into the usher coat, neatly, as if the fine were paid by listening. Last beat: she stamps the party's air with the compact, a blessing this time, and the hidden landing's icon fades from even the private directory.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A clasped compact and a ribbon that only ties itself when an oath is finished. No series prop, no stat.

research.originalInspiration: Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent of Norse mythology
facts: Jörmungandr, also called the Midgard Serpent or World Serpent, is an immense sea serpent in Norse mythology who encircles the earth and bites his own tail. Letting go of the tail is named as a sign that Ragnarök is beginning.
The Prose Edda account summarized on the page: Odin cast the serpent into the ocean around Midgard, and it grew large enough to circle the world and grasp its tail.

One preserved story has Thor lift the serpent while it is disguised as a cat, raising it only enough for one paw to leave the floor. Another has Thor hook it while fishing. At Ragnarök, Thor kills the serpent and then dies of its venom.
This fight uses the circle and the letting-go as a floor's image. It does not stage the gods, the fishing trip, or the end of the world.

sources.title: Jörmungandr
sources.supports: World-encircling serpent biting its tail; releasing the tail as a sign of Ragnarök; vast scale.

creative.nameTh: เซอร์ขดด้าย
creative.visualIdentity: A serpent of tape and scale buckled around the tower's unfinished waist. One end is a clasp biting the other. The portrait row is wrapped by one continuous body that still resolves into four seats: clasp, two held-tail segments, one loose end. A tailor's chalk marks the measure.
creative.personality: Patient, enormous, and offended by a building that will not hold still.
creative.signatureTrait: The closed circle. The phase is the clasp letting go, drawn as a change of outline, not as the end of the world.
creative.comedyConcept: Absurd comedy at epic scale. The world serpent is trying to finish the tower's waist measurement, and the hunters are standing in the number.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: The clasp seat Taunts. The held-tail seats Shield and Regen the clasp, a circle feeding itself with existing ally effects. The loose-end seat holds ATK cards and is hard to choose while Taunt is up. No poison status exists, and none is added.
creative.weaknessConcept: The clasp is the legal target. When it falls, the held-tail seats are what the circle was hiding, and the loose end is already on the board. Players who only scratch segments while the clasp lives are measuring the wrong end.
creative.loreSummary:
A tower anomaly belted around the scaffolding where the Mysterious Tower was never finished. Hunters see it from other floors as a weather of tape and scale. The battle is still one party against four seats. Beating it does not move the sea or start a doom. It lets the waist be a hallway again.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Sir Yarncoil is a tower anomaly belted around the Roof Garden of Indoor Weather, still trying to measure the Mysterious Tower's waist. Letting the clasp go makes a hallway again, and it starts no doom and no quest.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy world serpent of tailor's tape and pale scales, clasp biting its tail around a ring of unfinished stone. Four clear segments for four seats, one illustration. Chalk marks. No thunder god, no fishing boat. Silhouette wraps the card frame: circle first, clasp as the break in the circle.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-11 The Roof Garden of Indoor Weather. The waist of the Mysterious Tower, a belt of weather around the open roof.

boss.bossTitle: Waist of the Unfinished Tower / เอวหอคอยที่ยังไม่เสร็จ
boss.entranceConcept: The plate is wider than the four portraits. The coil is shown closed around the frame, then settles into four seats. One line: the measure is short. A tower-wide banner is presentation copy for the floor, not a new map system and not a shared health bar.
boss.signatureSilhouette: A ring bigger than one portrait, clasp as the only asymmetry. At card size the ring alone must read. The chalk is secondary.
boss.personalityMotivation: The tower grew a floor without telling the belt. He will hold the waist shut until the number comes out even. Hunters are surplus cloth.
boss.signatureMechanic: Clasp Taunt. Segment Shield and Regen on allies. Loose-end ATK waiting behind the taunt. Pattern B, all four present at the start. Concepts only, no amounts. World scale is the illustration and the rarity of the floor, not a second rule set.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern B. When the clasp is gone, the art opens from a circle into a vertical strike and the remaining seats are the loose measure. Regen from the held tail stops mattering because those seats are the ones dropping. The chalk marks stay so the body is still the belt. Letting go is a floor measurement, a mark on the landing.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: The tape goes slack and pools down the scaffold like a measuring ribbon that finally reached the end. Scales click into a heap of buckles. Last beat: the chalk mark is one notch past the stone, and he flicks it, annoyed, as the ring becomes a hallway.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A scale buckle and a tailor's chalk that only marks stone. Trophy of having been at the waist. No stats.

research.originalInspiration: Umibōzu, the giant black sea figure of Japanese folklore who demands a ladle
facts: The English Wikipedia page, fetched 2026-11-20, says umibōzu, literally 'sea monk', is a yōkai in the form of a giant black human-like being. The literal gloss is recorded here and is not the creature's name in the creative block.

The page says it appears to sailors on calm seas that then turn rough. It breaks the ship as it rises, or it demands a ladle and drowns the crew. The told escape is to give it a bottomless ladle and sail while it is confused.

The page says it typically reveals only its upper body. Near-synonyms include umihōshi and uminyūdō. Some tellings call it the ghost of a drowned priest. That reading, the drowning, and the shapeshifting assault tales further down the page are not used.

sources.title: Umibōzu
sources.supports: Giant black human-like yōkai; calm sea turning rough; ladle demand; bottomless ladle as the escape; often only the upper body.

creative.nameTh: ดามกระบวยรั่ว
creative.visualIdentity: Only the upper body fits in the frame, black, wider than the doorway, a wooden ladle with the bottom already punched out held forward like a seal. Three small spoons with no bowls share the other seats. No robes. No shaved head. No shipwreck.
creative.personality: Polite, enormous, and confused by holes.
creative.signatureTrait: The ladle with no bottom. A shield is the answer the story already allows.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous at world scale. A giant asks the cellar for a ladle, and the only ladle in the building already has a hole.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: She Taunts, because she is waiting for an answer. The scoop is an ATK. A party Shield, from an ordinary DEF, is the bottomless reply: the scoop spends itself on a shield that does not fill. Her Skill is a self Taunt plus a self DEF buff, the moment she peers into the hole and braces. No new damage type.
creative.weaknessConcept: The hole. On the peer turn she makes herself the legal target and she is not scooping. Smoke, tobacco, and any clerical weakness are not used.
creative.loreSummary:
A Wild Creature whose upper half rises where a cellar ceiling already failed. The calm light, then the harsh light, is the entrance. The card calls the figure a tide giant. The fight is still four seats.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Dame Dryladle is a wild giant in the Basement of Retired Bosses, asking for a ladle that already has a hole. She is not one of the retired bosses, and the fifteen biomes include no sea, so the open ceiling does the work.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy world-boss plate, a black giant from the waist up, too wide for the door, a wooden ladle whose bowl is a bright hole, three tiny bottomless spoons. Grand bulk. No clerical robes, no tonsure, no drowning, no sailors, no statue-head comparison. Silhouette: a mass cut by the top of the frame, and a circle with a hole.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-10 The Basement of Retired Bosses. Partial fit only. See notes.environmentConflict. The Mysterious Tower has no sea biome in the fifteen.

boss.bossTitle: The Giant Who Asked for a Ladle / ยักษ์ที่ขอกระบวย
boss.entranceConcept: Wide plate. The room is calm. The upper body rises until the ladle taps the broken ceiling. One line: a ladle, please. Later visits: the rise and the line. The light change is presentation, not a new system.
boss.signatureSilhouette: Upper body only, black bulk wider than the frame, a ladle held forward as a circle with a bright hole. The hole is the primary characteristic. Facing is the ladle.
boss.personalityMotivation: She asked for a ladle, because that is the request in the story. The tower's ladle already had no bottom, because that is the told way through. She is still checking the hole. Hunters are the people in the room while she checks.
boss.signatureMechanic: Taunt on the demand. Scoop is an ATK. Self card: Taunt plus DEF buff, the peer into the hole. Pattern A. Spoon seats are present and only DEF. A party Shield is an existing DEF, not a new item. No amounts.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. After the peer, the room's light goes harsh, the calm turning rough as a lighting change, and the scoop cards lead. The upper body and the holed ladle stay, so the change does not erase him. No second health bar.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: She scoops. The hole was already there. She looks through it, finds the room still occupied, and lowers herself under the floor line. Last beat: the ladle stands upright in a puddle, bottom missing, polite.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A wooden ladle with the bottom already out, and a splinter of ceiling. Trophy objects only, no stats.

research.originalInspiration: Behemoth, the beast described in Job 40
facts: Behemoth is a beast from the Book of Job, described on the page as an echo of primeval chaos-monsters, and the name is used metaphorically for any extremely large or powerful thing. The Hebrew form is an augmentative of the word for beast.

Job 40, as quoted on the page: he eats grass like cattle; strength is in the loins and the belly; the tail stands like a cedar; bones are like tubes of bronze and limbs like iron rods; he is the first of God's works and only his maker can draw the sword against him; he lies under lotuses and swamp reeds; the passage asks whether he can be taken by the eyes or his nose pierced by hooks.
The page pairs him in later tradition with the sea-monster Leviathan. This record does not require that pair.
Later images, including a demon in the Dictionnaire Infernal and a speaking cat in a modern novel, are different characters and are not the reference.

sources.title: Behemoth
sources.supports: Job 40: grass-eating bulk, cedar-like tail, bronze bones, lotus and reed bed, unhookable nose.

creative.nameTh: เซอร์ทุ่งบัว
creative.visualIdentity: A hippo-shouldered, ox-heavy beast lying across the loading dock, tail a bundle of packing tubes stood up like a cedar, hide stitched with bronze-colored strapping. He eats flattened cardboard the way the verse says grass. Lotus stamps mark the crates he lies under. The snout is ringless.
creative.personality: Sleepy, courteous, and immovable. He apologizes for the space he takes and does not yield it.
creative.signatureTrait: The unhooked snout and the lying-down mass. Standing up is the phase.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. The primeval beast of the reed bed has made a bed of packing paper and will not be winched.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: Two grazer seats Regen him, the cardboard diet. His snout seat Taunts: the hook-point is where blows have to go. His body seat Shields, the bronze-bone bulk as a shield pool. An on-attack passive may add bonus_damage once the grazers are gone, the standing trample. No sword-of-the-maker mechanic.
creative.weaknessConcept: The snout is the taunting seat, so the party is already aimed at the place the verse asks about hooks. Grazers are the regen source. When they fall, the stand-up happens and the shield story thins because those seats were the ones feeding him. No hook item is added to the deck.
creative.loreSummary:
A Wild Creature who came up through the dock reeds of packing paper and lay down where the tower receives its crates. Hunters see the tubes of the tail from the stair. The fight is one party and four seats. He is not Leviathan's partner in this tower, and he is not an Aegis tank.

Lore link (agent 08, PROPOSED): Sir Lotusbulk is a wild beast asleep on packing paper in the Menagerie of Unfiled Beasts, too courteous to be winched. The dock is a prop in that pen, and he is not an Aegis tank.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy colossal beast lying across a dock, bronze straps, packing-tube tail upright, lotus-stamped crates, ringless snout, cardboard in the mouth. Huge relative to the portraits, gentle eye. Not a dinosaur reconstruction, not an elephant demon, not a cat. Silhouette: low vast body, vertical tail bundle, snout forward.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-08 The Menagerie of Unfiled Beasts. A pen in the Mysterious Tower whose labels he has eaten. Lotus crates are props, not a new dock biome.

boss.bossTitle: Unhookable Beast of the Dock / อสูรท่าขนของที่เบ็ดไม่ติด
boss.entranceConcept: Wide plate. He is already lying down, which is the point: the dock was the boss before the UI finished drawing. One line, drowsy: the hook will not hold. The tail of tubes rises last, so the cedar shape reads.
boss.signatureSilhouette: A horizontal mass wider than four portraits, a vertical bundle tail, a snout with no ring. Bulk reads as the threat. The lotus stamp is secondary.
boss.personalityMotivation: He was first in the dock and sees no reason to become second. Hunters may cross if they can convince the snout. He is not angry. He is in the way on a cosmic scale.
boss.signatureMechanic: Snout Taunt. Body Shield. Grazer Regen. Pattern B, four seats at the start: snout, body, two grazers. Standing trample is the on-attack bonus after the grazers are gone. No amounts.
boss.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern B. When both grazers fall, he stands in the art: the horizontal mass becomes a vertical one, tubes still the tail. Shield was the lying story; the remaining seats' ATK cards are the standing story. The snout stays ringless so the identity holds. No new size stat.
boss.defeatAnimationConcept: He kneels back into the cardboard reeds, tubes fanning out and then lowering. The snout dips, still unringed. Last beat: he nudges a lotus crate upright, as if tidying the dock he occupied, and the eye shuts.
boss.uniqueLootTheme: A bronze strap and a lotus dock-seal. Hide is not a stat material in this record.
